description.narrative: (Haiti): USAID/Haiti's food fortification project (RANFOSE), co-funded by HIV funding, continues to improve health and nutrition outcomes by addressing micronutrient deficiencies and food fortification. Micronutrient deficiencies are a major challenge in Haiti. Based on the 2016-2017 Demographic Health Survey data, 66 percent of children under five are anemic, as are 49 percent of women of reproductive age. The RANFOSE project works with importers, distributors, and local food producers to fortify wheat flour with iron and folic acid, vegetable oil with vitamin A, and salt with iodine. Through the support of this activity, Vitamin A fortified oil was introduced for the first time in the Haitian market...FY 2022 resources will continue to be used to:..Increase the availability of high-quality, fortified staple foods across the country by expanding local production and increasing imports of fortified foods, .Provide clear, consistent, and useful messaging for wholesale and retail consumers on the value and safety of fortified foods. .Continue and extend media campaigns that encourage the use of fortified foods, including cooking oil fortified with Vitamin A, iodized salt, and fortified wheat flour..Continue to support the National Food Quality Laboratory, which provides testing to assure that micronutrients are present at the stated levels in fortified foods. ..The project will continue to strengthen the capacity of the Government of Haiti to address critical issues related to sustained and effective food fortification programs. RANFOSE directly supports and contributes to the government-led efforts to improve the nutrition, health, and food security of the Haitian population..
